- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is below recent low, adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid underestimating bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is above recent high, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overestimating bearish reversal.  
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline, reduce peak value by 5–10% to account for overreaction.  
- If forecast mean is consistently below true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias to correct for mean reversion bias.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3 or more) and forecast is smooth, introduce 1–2% volatility adjustment to match sentiment-driven noise.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, apply a 1–2% upward correction to avoid horizon decay bias.
